title: Which Weather Model Is Most Accurate? We Score Them Every Day, in the Open
gist: VIDRAFT launched an open, daily-updated Global Weather Model Leaderboard on Hugging Face scoring physics and AI forecast models against ERA5 across 24 cities, plus its own fusion system Darwin-Prediction-Weather. The 2026 record shows AI models (ECMWF AIFS, NOAA AIGFS) beating their physics counterparts at every lead time, and VIDRAFT claims its skill-weighted fusion model leads all four elements at 1-7 days and all 15 WeatherBench 2 cells (self-reported).

insights.claim: VIDRAFT argues that small forecast improvements (one degree closer or one day earlier) change real decisions for farmers, grid operators buying power, airlines holding flights, and cities opening shelters, making weather a field where accuracy and economic value meet in one number.
insights.speaker: VIDRAFT_LAB
insights.so_what: Forecast accuracy directly feeds energy procurement, agriculture, and aviation operations, so better models have monetizable value.
insights.quote: Weather prediction is one of the few fields where accuracy, science and economic value meet in the same number.
insights.locator: A forecast that is one degree closer

insights.claim: In the last three years a new generation of AI weather models trained on historical weather has arrived and now runs side by side with supercomputer physics models at the world's weather centres.
insights.speaker: VIDRAFT_LAB
insights.so_what: Signals a structural shift in how national weather services produce forecasts, with implications for supercomputer demand versus AI compute.
insights.locator: For decades, weather forecasts have come from physics

insights.claim: In the 2026 year-to-date record across 24 cities, ECMWF's AI model AIFS has lower error than ECMWF's physics model IFS at every lead time, and NOAA's AIGFS beats NOAA's GFS at every lead time.
insights.speaker: VIDRAFT_LAB
insights.so_what: Independent operational evidence that AI forecasters now outperform the flagship physics models of the two largest weather centres.

insights.claim: The Global Weather Model Leaderboard records daily what each model predicted for 24 cities on six continents up to 10 days ahead, scores daily max/min temperature, max wind and precipitation by RMSE against ERA5 reanalysis, and only compares models on days and cities where all issued forecasts.
insights.speaker: VIDRAFT_LAB
insights.so_what: An open, continuously updated benchmark lets users judge model vendors on current-year operational skill rather than past papers.

insights.claim: The leaderboard's record begins 1 January 2026, and forecasts 8 to 10 days ahead will enter the ranking only as their target days are verified; planned additions include station-observation scoring, more cities and elements, and a public forecasting game.
insights.speaker: VIDRAFT_LAB
insights.so_what: Current rankings are limited to 1-7 day leads and 24 cities, so conclusions on longer ranges are still pending.

insights.claim: VIDRAFT's Darwin-Prediction-Weather produces a single forecast by skill-weighted fusion of global forecasts with local correction for temperature and wind, learning only from days whose observed value was known before the scored forecast.
insights.speaker: VIDRAFT_LAB
insights.so_what: Ensemble/fusion over public model output is a low-cost path to state-of-the-art skill, which could commoditize single-model forecast vendors.

insights.claim: On VIDRAFT's own leaderboard, Darwin-Prediction-Weather has the lowest RMSE in all four elements at every lead time from 1 to 7 days, with ECMWF AIFS second in every cell; for daily max temperature it scores 0.84 C at 1 day versus AIFS 1.35 C, and 2.09 C at 7 days versus 2.41 C.
insights.speaker: VIDRAFT_LAB
insights.so_what: Self-reported results on a board run by the same team; the margin over AIFS is large for temperature and wind but thin for precipitation.

insights.claim: Darwin-Prediction-Weather's precipitation advantage is marginal, with RMSE of 4.15 mm versus AIFS 4.33 mm at 1 day and 7.11 mm versus 7.30 mm at 7 days, compared with much larger gaps for wind (2.25 vs 3.60 km/h at 1 day).
insights.speaker: VIDRAFT_LAB
insights.so_what: Precipitation remains the hardest element; fusion gains concentrate in temperature and wind, relevant for energy demand and wind-power forecasting.

insights.claim: VIDRAFT says the same engine records the lowest error in all 15 evaluated cells of Google Research's WeatherBench 2 2020 deterministic protocol (2 m temperature, Z500 and T850 at 1-10 days), e.g. 0.468 K vs 0.488 K best official at 1-day 2 m temperature, and has submitted the entry to the WeatherBench 2 team.
insights.speaker: VIDRAFT_LAB
insights.so_what: Claim awaits official WeatherBench 2 verification; margins are small (a few percent), so treat as provisional.
insights.locator: The same engine was also evaluated on WeatherBench 2

insights.claim: A Darwin-27B model with a calibrated readout serves as a decision core that turns forecast fields into decisions such as go/no-go, threshold exceedance and category probabilities.
insights.speaker: VIDRAFT_LAB
insights.so_what: Points to a productization path selling decision support, not raw forecasts, to weather-sensitive businesses.

insights.claim: The leaderboard app is Apache 2.0 licensed, but the compiled daily record and the Darwin-Prediction-Weather model are CC BY-NC 4.0, non-commercial only, with commercial use requiring contact with VIDRAFT.
insights.speaker: VIDRAFT_LAB
insights.so_what: The open-data framing masks a commercial licensing model; enterprises cannot use the model or data without a deal.
